This land is my own, and I have farmed sorghum on it for many years. The rains here in the North East come only once, so I plant with the first good rains in June and hope they last through September. I will intercrop with cowpea as I always do — it helps the soil and feeds my family. I do not have much money, so I will use the seed I kept from last harvest, put a little NPK if the agro-dealer has the subsidized bag, and add manure from my goats. For weeding I will work with my sons, and hire two or three young men for a few days when the grass gets heavy.
